questions.questionText: Why do LLMs use subword tokenization instead of splitting text into whole words?
options: Whole-word tokenization needs a huge vocabulary and has no good way to handle words never seen during training
Subword tokenization is simpler to implement, nothing else
LLMs cannot process whole words at all
It has no real advantage, it's purely a historical accident
questions.correctAnswer: Whole-word tokenization needs a huge vocabulary and has no good way to handle words never seen during training
questions.explanation: Subword tokenization lets common words be single tokens while unseen/rare words can still be represented as familiar sub-pieces, avoiding the "unknown word" problem entirely.

questions.questionText: What does Byte-Pair Encoding's merge step actually do?
options: It repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair of tokens across the training data into a new single token
It removes rare words from the vocabulary entirely
It translates text into a different language
questions.correctAnswer: It repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair of tokens across the training data into a new single token
questions.explanation: BPE builds its vocabulary bottom-up: starting from individual characters, it repeatedly finds and merges the most frequent adjacent pair, growing common patterns into single tokens.

questions.questionText: Why does token count matter practically when using an LLM API, beyond just understanding how the model works internally?
options: It doesn't matter practically, only word count matters for billing
API pricing, rate limits, and the maximum context window are all measured in tokens, not words or characters
Token count only matters for training, never for using an existing model
Tokens are only relevant for non-English languages
questions.correctAnswer: API pricing, rate limits, and the maximum context window are all measured in tokens, not words or characters
questions.explanation: Since billing, rate limits, and context window size are all denominated in tokens, understanding roughly how text maps to token count is practically useful even without training your own model.
